CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Vice Mayor Madison presented a proclamation declaring the week of
  October 20-26, 2024, as National Friends of the Libraries Week, and
  expressed gratitude to the City's Library staff and the Friends of the
  Library organization for supporting learning opportunities for individuals
  of all ages and promoting positive civic engagement. Janice Siegel
  accepted the proclamation, on behalf of the Friends of the Library, and
  emphasizing the importance of public libraries and they opportunities
  they open. Christine Reader, Adult Services Librarian, thanked the
  Friends of the Library for their volunteerism and supporting learning
  opportunities for the community.

  Vice Mayor Madison presented a proclamation proclaiming the month
  of October 2024 as Bullying Prevention Awareness Month, and
  expressed gratitude to the Pasadena Youth Network and their efforts
  to raise awareness on the negative impacts of bullying. Lola Osborne,
  Deputy Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Services, spoke
  on the importance of respecting one another and to prevent bullying.

  Vice Mayor Madison presented a proclamation recognizing Red Ribbon
  Week 2024, reaffirming the City's commitment to preventing substance
  abuse and promoting the well being of all residents. Christy Zamani and
  Claudia Hathcock, Day One, accepted the proclamation, thanked the
  City Council for the recognition, sharing details on the upcoming
  National Drug Take Back Day event on October 26, 2024.

Council Minutes  2  10/21/2024
   Vice Mayor Madison presented a certificate of commendation to City
  Attorney/City Prosecutor Michelle Bagneris for her 25 years of service
  to the City, and spoke on her numerous accomplishments spanning
  over two decades. City Attorney Bagneris thanked the City Council for
  their continued support and expressed her gratitude for the opportunity
  to serve the City of Pasadena.

  Vice Mayor Madison requested the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of Maddalena Riboli from the iconic San Antonio Winery and Sharp
  Seating in Pasadena, and spoke on her vital role as a leading woman
  in the American wine industry.

  Vice Mayor Madison also requested for the meeting to be adjourned
  in memory of Trader Joe's founder and Pasadena resident, Alice
  Coulombe, noting her many roles and contributions to the City.

  Samuel Blumberg, Pasadena resident, requested for the City Council
  to consider a letter of support that Pasadena does not support hate or
  bigotry.

  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident, advocated for charter change to
  give more oversight of the Police Department to the City Council, and
  spoke on AB392.

  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident, reflected on his community activism,
  spoke on improving the community, and provided other various
  comments.

  Maria Castellon, Commission on the Status of Women, announced
  details for the upcoming Light a Candle Event on Thursday, October
  24, 2024 in honor of Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

  Jill Thompson, Commission on the Status of Women, spoke on the
  importance of raising awareness regarding domestic violence, uplifting
  the voices of survivors, and helping them heal.

  Monet Bagneris, Pasadena resident, warmly congratulated City
  Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris on her 25 years o1
  service to the City and her amazing accomplishments during that time.

  SHOPPERS LANE PARKING LOTS (Transportation Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is statutorily
  exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15273 (Rates, Tolls, Fares, and
  Charges);
  (2) Direct the City Attorney to prepare and return with an ordinance
  within 60 days consistent with the provisions set forth in the Agenda
  Report amending Pasadena Municipal Code Chapter 10.45.225 (South
  Lake Parking Meter Zone) to:
  a. Adopt an occupancy-based parking meter rate and
  authorize the Director of Transportation to adjust the base
  parking rate at no less than $1.00 per hour and no greater
  than $5.00 per hour as permitted by posted parking
  regulations.
  i. The rates shall be based on parking demand, with the
  goal of reaching occupancy by vehicles at the rate of
  70 to 90 percent for parking meter spaces on each
  block at such times and hours that payment is
  required;
  ii. Rate changes will not occur more than once every six
  months;
  iii. As defined in the agenda report, adopt an escalated
  parking meter rate allowing the Director of
  Transportation to set the escalated parking rate to be
  up to two times the base meter rate for any parking
  beyond an initial base parking period; and
  iv. Beginning on July 1, 2025, and on each July 1,
  thereafter, the maximum rates shall be raised by an
  amount equal to the change in the consumer price
  index and rounded down to the nearest quarter of a
  dollar; and
  (3) Adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 General
  Fee Schedule to adopt new rates for the Shoppers Lane Parking Lots
  (Resolution No. 10092).
  Recommendation of the South Lake Parking Place Commission:
  On March 23, 2023, the South Lake Parking Place Commission
  unanimously recommended that the City Council approve the following
  changes to parking rates in the South Lake area, as further detailed in
  the body of the Agenda Report:
  South Lake Parking Meters - On-street
  • Adopt an occupancy-based parking rate structure similar to the
  one adopted for the Playhouse Parking Meter Zone.
  • Adopt an escalated parking rate.
  • Each fiscal year, raise the maximum rates by CPI.

Council Minutes  7  10/21/2024
   Shoppers Lane Parking Lots
  • Eliminate the 90-minute free period and replace with a
  validation program for merchants.
  • Adopt an occupancy-based parking rate structure for the lots.
  • Raise the daily maximum rate to $12.
  • Extend the hours of operation of the Shoppers Lane lots to 24
  hours a day, 7 days a week.
  • Each fiscal year, raise the maximum rates by CPI.
  The SLPPC revisited and unanimously reaffirmed their recommend
  rate changes in May of 2024.

OLD BUSINESS  RECREATION AND PARKS COMMISSION: PROPOSED OPTIONS
  TO RECOGNIZE RHYTHM AND BLUES (R&B) MUSIC GROUP
  TROOP (Public Works Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed options in the agenda report to recognize
  Troop are categorically exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) under Section 15061(b)(3), "Common Sense"
  exemption that CEQA only applies to projects that have the potential
  for causing a significant effect on the environment; as well as under
  Section 15301 as a minor alteration of an existing facility with no
  change in capacity; and
  (2) Review and select amongst four proposed options to recognize
  rhythm and blues (R&B) music group, Troop; or
  (3) Provide alternate direction.
  Recommendation of the Recreation and Parks Commission: On
  October 1, 2024, four proposed options were presented to the
  Recreation and Parks Commission along with relevant background
  information. The Commission unanimously supported Option 'D' to
  install a plaque on the exterior wall at the entrance to the Pasadena
  Civic Auditorium.

  Kris Markarian, Acting Director of Public Works, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item, provided background information
  on the project and the process, presented recognition options, and
  responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 3 letters advocating for the City Council
  to honor Troop in various ways (renaming the dance room at the Jackie
  Robinson Center, a street named after the group, a plaque at Pasadena
  High School, and/or by placing a plaque at the Civic Center), and 10
  letters in opposition to the City renaming Dayton Street, including 1
  letter/petition with 39 signatures in opposition to the City renaming
  Dayton Street, were received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to
  the City Council, posted on line, and made part of the public record for
  this item.

REPORTS AND  SUPPORT OF PROPOSITION 36, "ALLOWS FELONY CHARGES
COMMENTS FROM  AND INCREASES SENTENCES FOR CERTAIN DRUG AND THEFT
COUNCIL COMMITTEES  CRIMES" ON THE NOVEMBER 6, 2024 STATE GENERAL
  ELECTION BALLOT (Office of the City Manager)
Legislative Policy  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
Committee  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is covered by
  the "Common Sense" exemption set forth in State CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061 (b )(3) as CEQA only applies to projects that may have a
  significant effect on the environment; and
  (2) Support Proposition 36 on the November 5, 2024, state ballot.

  Alex Hernandez, Assistant to the City Manager, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item, provided a brief overview of
  Proposition 36, and responded to questions.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding how
  Proposition 36 aligns with the City's legislative platform, Assistant to
  the City Manager Hernandez reported that the areas in alignment
  pertain to public safety and quality of life issues.

  In response to Councilmember Williams' inquiry regarding financial
  costs of implementation of Proposition 36, City Manager Marquez
  reported that the County and/or State could potentially face costs for
  prosecution and providing a defense.

  Councilmember Rivas expressed concerns related to the unfunded
  indirect costs that the measure would create, such as treatment for
  certain individuals with drug offenses.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiries regarding drug
  offenses, City Prosecutor Tim Wellman reported that the if Proposition
  36 were passed by voters, the District Attorney's Office would have the
  discretion to charge a person in possession of illegal drugs as a felony
  if the person has two or more prior drug possessions, or other drug
  related offenses.

Council Minutes  15  10/21/2024
   Vice Mayor Madison expressed concerns regarding Proposition 36,
  stating that it does not provide adequate funding for treatment, and may
  be unfairly applied to individuals based on race and ethnicity, and
  potentially lead to unfortunate consequences.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition of the proposed state
  ballot measure Proposition 36 and/or provided other various
  comments:

  Margaret diZerega, Vera Institute of Justice
  Selina Ho, Vera Institute of Justice
  Jess Farris, ACLU of Southern California

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that two letters advocating for the City
  Council to oppose Proposition 36 and providing comments on the
  matter, and two letters (submitted for the Legislative Policy Committee
  meeting) advocating for the City to oppose Proposition 36 which risks
  budget cuts from LA County Programs, were received by the City
  Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted online, and made
  part of the public record for this item.

  Councilmember Lyon expressed opposition Proposition 36, stating that
  the measure is a reaction to the uptick in shoplifting and property crimes
  in the past two years, noting that property crimes are still at a historically
  low point.

  MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Lyon, seconded
  by Councilmember Rivas, to oppose state Proposition 36.

  In response to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry regarding why there
  should be support for Proposition 36, City Attorney Bagneris noted that
  supporting arguments for the measure state that tougher laws and
  penalties may serve as a deterrent to committing crimes. Chief
  Assistant City Prosecutor Wellman added that under Proposition 36
  individuals may be given an admonition, while if an individual is
  convicted of selling drugs such as fentanyl, and someone dies from
  those drugs, that person could be prosecuted for second degree
  murder.

  Discussion ensued regarding the opportunity of treatment, lack of
  funding for treatment, wobblers, and the District Attorney's policies.

 SUBSTITUTE MOTION:  Following additional discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Williams, seconded by Councilmember Hampton, to take no position.
  (Motion unanimously approved) (Absent: Mayor Gordo)
